Definition: A control where a person types a single line of text.
The blinking line that shows where the next letter you type will go. It is sometimes called the text cursor.
Checking what a person typed before the program uses it, for example making sure a box is not empty.
How correct, complete and usable a piece of data is. A name typed with extra spaces, or a box left empty, is a data quality problem.
An object that a control calls when something happens to it. A TextChangeListener is called each time the text changes.
A text field that hides what is typed, showing stars instead of the letters.
When a rule or program treats some groups of people unfairly, often by accident, for example a name check that rejects real names.
Something that protects people, data or devices. Some protect against people nearby, such as hiding a password on the screen; others protect data inside the computer.
